newsitem.title: USA: UAW, GM continue talking past strike deadline.
newsitem.headline: UAW, GM continue talking past strike deadline.

text.p: Bargainers for the United Auto Workers union agreed to continue contract talks past an 11:59 p.m. EDT deadline without a strike at a General Motors Corp. Milwaukee-area parts plant, a union spokesman said.
UAW spokesman Reg McGhee said the two sides agreed to continue discussions through the evening. A new strike deadline was not set.

About 900 workers from UAW Local 1866 had threatened to walk off the job at the Delphi Energy and Engine Management Systems plant in Oak Creek, Wis., if a new labor contract was not reached by the deadline.

The plant makes catalytic converters for many of GM's North American cars and trucks, as well as customers in Europe and Asia. Analysts have said a work stoppage could quickly affect GM's vehicle assembly operations.
Major issues in the talks include staffing levels, health and safety issues, long-term job security and subcontracting, a practice also known as outsourcing.

UAW members ratified a new national agreement with GM last fall. But the company has struggled to obtain new three-year contracts with its more than 100 UAW locals in the U.S. As of last week about 20 locals still did not have new agreements.
Since the beginning of this year the company has been hit by a total of five strikes -- three by UAW members and two by members of the International Union of Electronic Workers.

One of those strikes, a two-month-long walkout by UAW members at GM's Oklahoma City, Okla., car plant, badly marred the launch of the much anticipated redesigned Chevrolet Malibu and Oldsmobile Cutlass.

Union members, concerned over long-term term job security, have demanded that GM put a halt to outsourcing and add more jobs to relieve overtime strains. GM officials have said they need to produce cars and trucks more efficiently and cannot add excess workers.

GM faces two other strike deadlines Friday. About 900 workers at foundry in Saginaw, Mich., and 2,346 hourly workers at a Grand Rapids, Mich., stamping plant have both set deadlines of 11:59 p.m. (EDT) Friday for a new contract.
Talks also continued at GM's full-size pickup truck plant in Pontiac, Mich. About 5,700 members of UAW Local 594 have been on strike since April 22.
In a positive sign, a GM spokesman said bargainers talked until about 10 p.m. EDT Wednesday, about five hours longer than a typical day of negotiations.

CSM Forecasting Inc, a Farmington Hills, Mich., consulting firm, estimated that GM loses $8,200 for each unbuilt full-size pickup truck at Pontiac East. As of June 6, CSM said GM had lost 46,512 units. Nearly 90 percent of those were popular and profitable extended cab versions.
GM said last month the strikes at Oklahoma City and Pontiac East had cost it $225 million in lost profits. GM lost $1.2 billion in earnings to strikes in 1996.
